evidence: Publisher-deposited primary abstract and metadata opened; abstract explicitly states that the finite-vector-space conjecture of Rota is established. PDF transfer did not expose the text.

Bibliography opened and publication metadata checked. Primary ICM text was returned by search, including Definition, Central product theorem and Main theorem; opening the 47 MB proceedings PDF exceeded the retrieval limit. Result verification therefore records an indirect check, not a full-paper reading.

Author preprint, dated February 2002, opened. Hypotheses 1.0--1.1, Theorems A--B, Corollary C and the introduction were read. Publication metadata confirmed by the author bibliography search result. The theorem read treats the component case under the classification of finite simple groups; it is not silently generalized to characteristic two.
Full notes opened; Theorems 1.1 and 1.2, and the proof of the uniqueness theorem were read. No date is printed in the PDF; no date has been inferred from web crawl dates.

Publisher metadata opened together with full Russian translation, Matematika 13(4) (1969), 94--124. Theorem 2.5 and its proof, Lemma 4.1 and the product-state examples in section 4 were read. Original Annals record also opened.

Publisher abstract and metadata opened. The abstract explicitly states existence of the infinite-volume primary state for a finite-range one-dimensional quantum spin lattice, analyticity, and extremal KMS property. Full article was not accessible in this retrieval.
Tags 01X8 and 01XB opened. Lemmas 30.2.1--2 and the localization contracting-homotopy proof were read.
Tags 01XS and 01YR opened. Lemmas 30.8.1 and 30.14.1 and their proofs were read; the Noetherian hypothesis in the latter is explicit.

Original article opened from author institution. Affine acyclicity and affine-cover computation around pp. 238--240, projective finite-generation/vanishing and Euler characteristic sections inspected. Received 8 October 1954, printed March 1955.

Metadata and full four-page Russian paper opened via its PDF link. Sections 1--4, Claims 1--2 and Theorem 1 read. Received 21 October 1970. The original works over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field. It contains the exact canonical forms but not the seminar stability example.

Author preprint version 2, 16 August 2004, opened. Finite-dimensional Section 9, Theorems 9.1--9.2 and canonical forms on pp. 21--23 read; introduction graph encoding and Section 7 also checked. This reference is used for its explicit finite-dimensional results, not to identify the notebook with an infinite-dimensional problem.

Full English paper opened from the author webpage. Introduction and final four-subspace discussion, pp. 30--32, read. Received 18 December 1972. Used for the quiver translation and distinction between regular families and rigid cases, not as a source for an unlocated orbit-degeneration formula.
Section 59.69 and the proof of Lemma 59.69.3 read. It gives Picard group of a punctured smooth projective curve as the quotient by the classes of omitted points.

Original full paper opened. Proposition 3.1.8 on the logarithmic de Rham comparison and Theorem 3.2.5 on independence of compactification read. Received 15 September 1970; publication 1971. The received date does not by itself establish public circulation.

Publisher metadata opened; PDF access returned 403. The result was read in the introduction of Lupton--Phillips--Schochet--Smith, arXiv:math/0509269, where the Arens--Royden isomorphism is explicitly stated.

Full author preprint opened. Introduction, manuscript p. 2, explicitly states the Arens--Royden theorem for the invertible group and H1 of the maximal ideal space; the present citation uses that stated theorem, not the later rational-homotopy results.

Publisher metadata and full original Russian article, Funktsionalnyi Analiz i ego Prilozheniya 1(2), 91--92, opened. Theorem 1 on p. 91 gives the completed-curve criterion and the separate kernel/cokernel dimensions, hence negative winding for the conventional Fredholm index. Received 5 November 1966.

Publisher metadata and full Russian original, 4(3), 26--36, opened. Theorem 0.2, Theorem 6.1 on the quotient symbol algebra, and Theorem 7.1 on the negative-winding index were read. Received 5 June 1969; printed 1970. This is a related singular-integral algebra framework; Gohberg 1967 is the exact scalar Toeplitz theorem.

Sections 27.8 and 33.35, and Lemma 27.12.3 opened. The degree-zero localization construction, quotient-line-bundle interpretation of Proj, and Lemma 33.35.3 requiring a general hyperplane over an infinite field were read.

Curated primary author bibliography opened, entry 54. It identifies exactly the volume 16 reference in the notebook: proceedings of the Berkeley symposium of 1--26 July 1968, printed 1970. The original chapter was not successfully retrieved; mathematical vanishing was read in Bott 1976, sections 2 and 4.

Full author article opened. Section 2, pp. 125--126, gives the degree-truncated characteristic algebra; section 4, pp. 135--136, identifies its characteristic classes with those of the normal bundle TM/E and explicitly deduces the earlier vanishing obstruction.

Curated primary author bibliography opened, entry 46, with original abstract and publication metadata. Direct original full-text access failed; the exact holomorphic isolated-zero formula was read in Bruzzo--Rubtsov 2012, section 3.4, which cites this original.

Curated primary author bibliography opened, entry 45, with original abstract and publication metadata. The abstract distinguishes the earlier isolated nondegenerate-zero result from extensions to bundles and higher-dimensional nondegenerate zero loci. Full original article was not read in this run.

Full author manuscript v4, stamped 21 March 2012, opened; institution-hosted version and publication metadata also opened. Theorem 3.2, section 3.4 (manuscript p. 11), and section 4.5 Proposition 4.6 were read. This is actual result verification of the localization formula, distinct from metadata checking of the 1967 original. First preprint 11 October 2009; journal 2012.

Existing cumulative key reused. Official journal metadata opened in this run; no full-text reading is asserted here. It supports the historical identity of the theorem named in the notebook, not a new proof of the infinitesimal relation.

Primary publisher abstract and metadata opened. Received 4 February 1969, published 25 August 1969. Abstract explicitly attributes its infinite sequence of branch points and nonisolated origin to WKB analysis; full paper was not retrieved.

Author bibliography opened, entry 7, confirming title, journal, year, pages and appendix by A. Dicke. Publisher search text describes rigorous results and global three-sheeted monodromy, but opening the publisher full record/PDF returned 403; result verification is therefore indirect, not a full-paper reading.

Full Russian translation, Matematika 13(4) (1969), 94--124. Theorem 2.5 and proof, printed pp.100--101; Lemma 4.1 and examples, printed pp.113--114.
Lemma 30.2.2: arbitrary-ring affine acyclicity, using Lemma 30.2.1 localization contraction.

Section 59.69, proof of Lemma 59.69.3: Picard group of an open smooth curve is quotient by removed-point classes. Elliptic-point identification supplied as the classical pointed elliptic-curve specialization.
Lemma 33.35.3 and Remark 33.35.5: general hyperplane avoiding associated primes over an infinite field; exact twisted sequence.
Lemma 27.12.3: Proj represents generated invertible quotients, supporting the scheme-level projective interpretation.

Section 3.1, Proposition 3.1.8: logarithmic de Rham comparison; section 3.2, Theorem 3.2.5: compactification independence. Received 15 September 1970; journal year 1971 does not establish first public circulation date.

Version 2, section 9, Theorems 9.1--9.2 and listed normal forms, manuscript pp.21--23. Used to cross-check finite forms and the odd-zero correction, not to claim the exact P317 deformation had been located.

Full Russian original, pp.26--36; Theorems 0.2,6.1,7.1. Symbol quotient and negative winding; partial, broader-context match to the scalar Toeplitz example.
